tips.title: Select model body or component for machining
tips.body: Ensure the correct part is selected in the CAM setup to limit toolpath motion.

tips.title: Use Pocket/Contour Selections for 2D milling
tips.body: Select areas in which the tool can move (Pocket Selections) and areas that need material removed (Stock Contours).

tips.title: Use Machining Boundaries for 3D milling
tips.body: Limit toolpath motion to a particular area using Machining Boundaries (tool inside, center on, or outside boundary).

tips.title: Avoid using Stock Contours if not necessary
tips.body: If machining of only the pocket selection is desired, avoid defining Stock Contours for more efficient toolpaths.

tips.title: Use Slope containment for 3D finishing
tips.body: Limit motion by applying an allowable range of surface angles to the toolpath in all 3D finishing toolpaths.

tips.title: Use Model selections for interference avoidance
tips.body: Recognize bodies or surfaces by 3D toolpaths without adding them to the CAM Setup to avoid interference.

tips.title: Use Avoid/touch for multi-axis toolpaths
tips.body: Define surfaces to be machined or avoided during machining, avoiding the need for boundaries along the Z-axis.

tips.title: Avoid surfaces during multi-axis toolpaths
tips.body: Use 'Avoid Surfaces' in 3D strategies to prevent construction or fixture bodies from being machined.

tips.title: Automatic containment for Pencil and Horizontal toolpaths
tips.body: Pencil and Horizontal toolpaths use automatic containment, looking for internal fillets within a range defined by the tool size plus/minus the 'Overthickness' parameter.

tips.title: Rest Machining limits toolpaths based on stock definition options
tips.body: Rest Machining removes only remaining stock based on various stock definition options.

tips.title: Set cutting passes between Top and Bottom height definitions
tips.body: Limiting toolpaths along the Z-axis is done in the Heights tab for all milling toolpaths, generating passes between defined Top and Bottom heights.

tips.title: Select closed loops for model edges or sketch contours
tips.body: Fusion 360 defaults to selecting closed loops when choosing model edges or sketch contours.

tips.title: Edit selections using the Contour Editor
tips.body: Access the Contour Editor by hovering over a selection and clicking it again to edit model edges or sketch contours.

tips.title: Tolerance parameter controls mesh accuracy for toolpath generation
tips.body: The Tolerance parameter in Fusion 360 determines the allowable variance between true model geometry and the mesh as a chord distance.

tips.title: Smoothing parameter fits arc moves to toolpath within specified tolerance
tips.body: The Smoothing parameter in Fusion 360 adjusts the number of linear segments used for arcs, balancing output size, accuracy, and generation time.

tips.title: Troubleshooting toolpaths involves identifying, isolating, experimenting, and resolving issues
tips.body: Fusion 360 provides tools for troubleshooting CAM programs, including the Compare and Edit dialog to isolate variables.

tips.title: Toolpath warnings indicate changes to heights, ramping moves, or entry positions
tips.body: Warnings in Fusion 360 may indicate that toolpaths were automatically adjusted, such as lifting retract and clearance planes.

tips.title: Toolpath errors occur when toolpaths cannot be generated with current parameters
tips.body: Errors in Fusion 360 indicate issues like missing selections, irresolvable parameters, or unexpected errors during toolpath generation.

tips.title: Failed NC output occurs when post-processor cannot translate toolpath information
tips.body: A '.failed' file extension on the NC output file indicates that the post-processor is unable to translate Fusion 360 toolpath information into g-code.

tips.title: Use Compare and Edit to isolate variables in troubleshooting
tips.body: The Compare and Edit tool allows for easy identification of parameter differences between multiple toolpaths, aiding in troubleshooting.

tips.title: Use Compare and Edit to identify parameter differences
tips.body: Apply the 'different' toolpath parameters filter in the Compare and Edit dialog to isolate variables with different values.

tips.title: Adjust Minimum Cutting Radius (MCR) for efficient toolpaths
tips.body: Set a non-zero MCR value to prevent sharp corners and minimize chatter, while avoiding material removal in certain areas.

tips.title: Create derived operations for alternative toolpaths
tips.body: Right-click any existing operation in the MFG browser and select 'Create Derived Operation' to quickly create alternative strategies while maintaining the same parameters.

tips.title: Use defeatured models for cleaner roughing results
tips.body: Simplify models during the initial design process to avoid rollover and ensure clean results on curved walls.

tips.title: Avoid dropping into holes during surfacing operations
tips.body: Create a patch surface with curvature (G2) boundaries to force the toolpath to machine over the hole, avoiding unwanted drop-in.

tips.title: Use a machining boundary for side entry
tips.body: Create a machining boundary with 'Tool inside boundary' condition to avoid wraparound and air cutting on upper passes.

tips.title: Adjust toolpath tolerance for clean machining
tips.body: Reduce toolpath tolerance to 0.002" from default 0.004" to avoid issues with faceting in imported models.

tips.title: Use UV Diagnostic Tools for surface quality issues
tips.body: Access 'Texture Map Controls' and set Display Mode to 'UV Diagnostic Texture' to investigate inconsistencies in toolpath passes.

tips.title: Create a new surface to clean up UV isolines
tips.body: Use lofted t-spline/sculpted/form surfaces to create a cleaner surface that improves toolpath quality.

tips.title: Experiment with number of faces for accurate loft
tips.body: Adjust the number of faces in the loft to match the original model geometry accurately.
